name: NOFX
label: Epitaph
lede: Forty-one years, three original members, no major label, and a farewell that drew thousands to its home turf of San Pedro.

eras.title: Negative FX, minus the hardcore
eras.text: Three Los Angeles kids borrow a name from a Boston hardcore band and start a fast, jokey punk group. Lineup churn, a death in the ranks and a tiny local label mark the first four years.

years.cap: El Hefe playing trumpet with NOFX at The Observatory in Santa Ana, CA on Dece... · Wikimedia
years.h: Fat Mike, Eric Melvin and Smelly start a band in Los Angeles
years.p: Bassist and singer Mike Burkett, guitarist [[Eric Melvin|25a66564-3655-44a8-86be-c60fdf447b23]] and drummer Erik Sandin form NOFX, named after Boston hardcore band Negative FX.

years.h: Thalidomide Child demo, produced by Germs drummer Don Bolles
years.p: The band's first recording is produced by [[Don Bolles|538ca22d-da9b-4b4d-ba74-4244f327c72b]] of [[The Germs|42c4b58d-2e28-41d4-bfe5-4edee68386cf]]. Fat Mike later joked that nobody heard it until it was reissued in 2012.

years.h: Drummers come and go; guitarist Dave Allen dies in a car crash
years.p: Erik Sandin briefly leaves and Scott Sellers and Scott Aldahl fill in. New guitarist Dave Allen is killed in a car accident about four months after joining, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: First EP on Mystic Records
years.p: NOFX puts out its self-titled EP on the small Los Angeles label Mystic, followed by So What If We're on Mystic! in 1986.

years.h: Dave Casillas joins as second guitarist
years.p: Casillas gives NOFX its first two-guitar lineup, which records the band's debut album the following year.

eras.title: Epitaph moves in
eras.text: Brett Gurewitz of Bad Religion produces the first album, and his label Epitaph becomes NOFX's home for the next decade. A new guitarist, then a trumpet player, changes the sound.

years.h: Liberal Animation, produced by Bad Religion's Brett Gurewitz
years.p: NOFX's debut album is made with [[Brett Gurewitz|cd40188b-ea30-4729-bebb-e8c5091c9d02]] at the board and first appears on Mystic and Fat Mike's small Wassail label. Epitaph reissues it in 1991.

years.h: S&M Airlines, the first NOFX album on Epitaph
years.p: The band's second album arrives on Epitaph Records and sets the template of quick, melodic, wisecracking punk. Steve Kidwiller replaces Dave Casillas on guitar around the same time.

years.h: Fat Mike and Erin Burkett found Fat Wreck Chords in San Francisco
years.p: The label starts as a side project of NOFX's bassist and his wife and will grow into one of punk's biggest independents, home to [[Lagwagon|c7788fba-e635-4d8b-a937-01a68ab154e3]], [[Strung Out|0220a594-56a1-47ca-8288-001ead3a3546]] and [[No Use for a Name|d7bd0fad-2f06-4936-89ad-60c5b6ada3c1]].

years.h: Ribbed on Epitaph, with a new lead guitarist and trumpeter
years.p: [[El Hefe|06e0fdef-679a-403f-a8a7-f6bf2523959d]] (Aaron Abeyta) joins on lead guitar and trumpet, and Kidwiller leaves. He will stay for the rest of the band's life.

eras.title: Punk in Drublic, and a no to MTV
eras.text: NOFX becomes one of the biggest punk bands in America without a major label, radio hit or MTV. It turns down the majors in the liner notes and keeps making records on its own terms.

years.h: White Trash, Two Heebs and a Bean takes its name from the band
years.p: The title describes the members' backgrounds, and it is the first full album after El Hefe joined.

years.h: Punk in Drublic: 39 minutes that outsell everything
years.p: Recorded at Westbeach Recorders in Hollywood with Ryan Greene, it includes "Linoleum", "The Brews" and "Leave It Alone".
years.xp:
The title is a spoonerism of "Drunk in Public". It peaked at number 12 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and, six years after release, became NOFX's only RIAA gold record, per Wikipedia. A hidden bit at the end features El Hefe doing cartoon voices.

The song "Jeff Wears Birkenstocks" was written about an Epitaph employee, and Birkenstock made a short documentary about it in 2017.

years.h: "Leave It Alone" is on KROQ, but the video never goes to MTV
years.p: Fat Mike said the band made the video and decided not to send it to MTV because they did not want to be part of that machine.

years.h: Liner notes tell the major labels to leave them alone
years.p: The live album I Heard They Suck Live!! carries a note saying NOFX has done fine without the majors, and it stays independent.

years.h: Heavy Petting Zoo: first NOFX album on the Billboard chart
years.p: The record reaches number 63, and its vinyl edition, retitled Eating Lamb, is banned in Germany over its cover art.

years.h: The Decline: one 18-minute song, one political rant
years.p: NOFX releases The Decline, a single-track EP that runs about 18 minutes, among the longest punk songs ever released.

eras.title: Fat Mike's own label, and a war on Bush
eras.text: After the Epitaph years NOFX records for the label Fat Mike runs. Politics take over the band's public life, along with subscription vinyl and a TV tour diary.

years.h: Pump Up the Valuum closes the Epitaph chapter
years.p: NOFX's eighth album arrives in 2000 and is the last of its Epitaph run, after which the band works with Fat Wreck Chords.

years.h: The War on Errorism goes after George W. Bush
years.p: Fat Mike also organizes punkvoter.com and the Rock Against Bush compilations;
years.xp: Spin's oral history says the Rock Against Bush campaign raised $1 million for John Kerry, and that Bush's win in 2004 hit Fat Mike hard. Eric Melvin pointed to it as a possible breaking point for the band.

years.h: Wolves in Wolves' Clothing, after a 12-EP subscription club
years.p: It follows the 7-Inch of the Month Club, in which fans submitted cover art for a dozen EPs.

years.h: They've Actually Gotten Worse Live!! caps a TV tour
years.p: NOFX's world tour is filmed for the Fuse TV series Backstage Passport, and a second live album, recorded in San Francisco, follows on November 20.

eras.title: Cokie the Clown, a book and a bad night in Vegas
eras.text: The band gets its old members back on stage for its 25th anniversary, releases four more albums and a bestselling memoir, and Fat Mike takes a strange solo act on the road.

years.h: Kidwiller and Casillas rejoin for 25th-anniversary shows
years.p: Former guitarists Steve Kidwiller and Dave Casillas play San Diego, Hollywood and San Francisco with NOFX.

years.h: Coaster comes out
years.p: The band's eleventh album is followed in November by the Cokie the Clown EP.

years.h: Cokie the Clown plays SXSW; Fat Mike is banned from Emo's
years.p: Wikipedia reports Fat Mike's SXSW set as Cokie the Clown, and a stunt involving urine got him banned from the Austin club Emo's.
years.xp: A video showed Fat Mike urinating into a Patron bottle, then swapping in a clean one before the performance.

years.h: Self Entitled is NOFX's twelfth studio album
years.p: It follows a Great White North tour of Canada in 2011 and comes ahead of a 30th anniversary vinyl box set.

years.h: Fat Mike publishes NOFX: The Hepatitis Bathtub and Other Stories
years.p: The band's autobiography, written with Jeff Alulis, appears alongside the release of First Ditch Effort in October.

years.h: First Ditch Effort follows the single "Six Years on Dope"
years.p: It is NOFX's thirteenth studio album.

years.h: Vegas jokes cost NOFX a sponsor and a festival slot
years.p: After Eric Melvin and Fat Mike joked about the 2017 Las Vegas shooting, Stone Brewing dropped the band from its Punk in Drublic festival, and the band apologized.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Melvin joked about the shooting, and the band later called its remarks shitty and insensitive. NOFX and Me First and the Gimme Gimmes were removed from the Camp Punk in Drublic lineup.

eras.title: One last full lap
eras.text: A short run of late albums, a pandemic, and a final farewell that turns a punk band into a parade.

years.h: "Fish in a Gun Barrel" raises money for Moms Demand Action
years.p: The single answers mass shootings, with proceeds going to the gun-safety group.

years.h: Single Album arrives as the band's fourteenth studio record
years.p: Spin's oral history says pandemic recording was tense, with Fat Mike and Eric Melvin at odds over the band's direction.
years.xp: Spin's oral history says Fat Mike spoke about struggling with cocaine, opioids and alcohol, that the band held about three interventions, and that he was hospitalized in 2021 and went to rehab during the pandemic.

years.h: Fat Mike says NOFX will end in 2023
years.p: The band announces it will break up for its 40th anniversary, which Spin's oral history says Erik Sandin learned of as a surprise.

years.h: Double Album is the last full-length
years.p: It is NOFX's fifteenth and final studio album.

years.cap: NOFX performing in Uniondale, NY as part of Warped Tour '06 · Wikimedia
q: We've become one of those legacy bands.
years.h: Three last nights in San Pedro
years.p: NOFX plays its final shows at home in San Pedro, California, on October 4, 5 and 6, after 41 years.
years.xp: Spin put the crowd at about 15,000 people and NOFX premiered a new song, "We Did It Our Way", on the last night, described by Fat Mike as his thank-you to fans. Crowds on the farewell tour ran far bigger than the usual 2,000 to 3,000, according to the same account.

sources.title: Spin: NOFX's final days in their own words
